transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. I hope I'm not taking up time from someone who needs it more, but... well, I guess what finally brought me in is that I've just been feeling a little... off? 

I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I know I have a good life and a good career. It's just that the part of me that used to really reach out for people, and take pleasure in things... like my social work, my yoga practice, going to art galleries, or even just my journaling... it feels like it's gone very, very quiet lately. I'm mostly just, you know, moving through my obligations right now. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things the right way for you.
About how long have you been feeling this way?

Um, let me think... I'd say it's been about eight months? Give or take a little. It started right around the time we took my older relative into our apartment to live with us. 

I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining about them, or that I'm not happy to help family, because of course I am. I know how important caregiving is. But... I think that's when this whole shift in how I'm thinking, and how I'm working and connecting with people, really began. I suppose it's just been a bit of an adjustment having someone else in our space, and maybe I haven't handled the transition as perfectly as I should have. 

Does that seem like a reasonable explanation to you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right context for all this.
Have you ever experienced a period in your life before this where you felt this same way?

Um, no, actually. I don't think so. I mean, I've always tried to pride myself on being pretty resilient, you know? With my line of work, you really have to be. 

Of course, everyone has stressful weeks or times when they're just tired from working hard, but... this specific feeling of just being so, I don't know, disconnected from the things I usually love? No, this is definitely new for me. I've always been a very engaged and active person before all this. 

I hope that's a helpful answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of my history.
Along with losing interest in things, have you also been feeling persistently down, sad, or empty most days?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I've been feeling sad, exactly. Or empty. I mean, I know I have so much to be grateful for, and I really try to focus on the positive things in my life. 

I guess it's more just... a lack of energy for the things I used to enjoy? But I wouldn't call it feeling down or depressed. I'm still getting up and going to work and taking care of my family. I just... I don't feel that same spark, I suppose. 

Does that make sense? I don't want to make it sound worse than it is, because I know people go through much harder things. I just want to be accurate for you.
Over these past eight months, have you found yourself feeling persistently anxious or troubled by excessive worries that are hard to control?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, working in mental health myself, I definitely see what excessive worry looks like in my clients, and I really try to practice what I preach, you know? Keeping things in perspective and all that. 

Of course, I have normal everyday concerns—just wanting to make sure my relative is comfortable, or keeping up with my caseload at work—but it's nothing I can't control. I'm definitely not sitting around feeling anxious all day. I feel like I manage stress pretty well, all things considered. 

I hope that's reassuring? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns over these past several months?

Um, no, my sleep has been pretty normal, actually. I mean, I try to keep a very regular schedule—it's so important for good sleep hygiene, which I'm always telling my clients, so I have to make sure I'm doing it myself, right? 

I usually get to bed at a reasonable hour and wake up feeling fine. Maybe an occasional night where it takes me a little longer to drift off if I've had a busy day, but nothing out of the ordinary. I'm definitely getting enough rest to keep up with everything I need to do. 

Is that what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over these past eight months?

Um, no, not really. My appetite has been pretty steady, I think. I mean, I still make sure to eat balanced meals and everything. Working in the field, I know how important nutrition is for overall well-being, so I really try to stay on top of that. 

My weight hasn't really changed either, maybe just the normal pound or two fluctuation that everyone gets, but nothing major at all. I'm definitely still eating normally and taking care of myself. 

Does that sound okay? I hope I'm giving you the kind of information you need to hear.
Have you been feeling physically fatigued or lacking in energy nearly every day?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I've been feeling fatigued. I mean, sure, by the end of the week I might feel a little tired, but that's just normal for anyone working full-time and taking care of things at home, right? 

I definitely still have the energy to get through my days and be there for my clients and my relative. I make sure to pace myself and practice good self-care so I don't get burnt out. It's something I'm very mindful of. 

So, no, definitely not lacking energy every day. I hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure I'm doing okay.
Have you had any thoughts of death or thoughts that you would be better off not being here?

Oh, goodness, no. No, definitely not. I haven't had any thoughts like that at all. Um, I mean, working in mental health, I know exactly what to look out for with that kind of thing, and I know how serious it can be. So I promise you, if I ever felt like I'd be better off not being here, I would absolutely reach out for help and use my safety plan. 

But honestly, I appreciate my life and my work too much. I'm really trying my best to stay positive and keep moving forward, you know? I want to be here for my clients and my family.

I hope that's reassuring to hear? I just want to make sure you know I'm completely safe and doing everything I'm supposed to be doing.
